title: SLA matrix and dynamic rollout gates for mixed-latency workloads
creator: Leah Thompson
description: Goal: Define an actionable SLA/SLO matrix and automated rollout gate criteria that cover Redwood's mixed-latency workload classes (interactive chat, longform generation, embeddings, batch inference). This ticket captures product requirements, clarified scope, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating logic tied explicitly to error budget burn-rate, latency regressions, and regional availability. The output will feed the rollout orchestration and console runbooks used by SRE and platform teams.
background: Recent customer feedback and internal incidents show that a single SLO across all inference traffic hides class-specific regressions (e.g., chat latency spikes at low p99 while embeddings remain stable). We need class-aware SLOs plus dynamic rollout guards so model/version rollouts can progress safely without manual intervention for common failure modes. This also aligns with Dedicated and Private expectations for predictable throughput and contractual SLAs.
workload_classes: interactive_chat: low-token, latency-sensitive conversational requests; longform_generation: high-token, throughput-sensitive generation; embeddings: medium-latency, high-CPU/embedding cost; batch_inference: large-batched jobs with relaxed tail-latency requirements.
slo_matrix: Tiering: Free | Standard | Enterprise. For each workload-class and tier we define p50/p95/p99 latency targets (ms), availability (monthly), and allowed error-budget burn. Example (Standard): interactive_chat p50 < 40ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 500ms; longform_generation p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1500ms; embeddings p95 < 700ms; batch_inference p95 < 1200ms. Availability target (Standard): 99.95% monthly. Error budget: 0.05 of uptime per month (equivalent to 21.6 minutes of allowed downtime).
sli_definitions: Latency SLI: end-to-end server-side token latency measured at the Redwood ingress (exclude client-to-edge network). Availability SLI: 5xx + client-observed service rejections divided by total requests. Error budget burn: calculated on a rolling 30-day window and represented as burn rate relative to expected budget.
rollout_gates: Staged rollout policy for model/version changes: 1) Canary phase: route 1% traffic for 30-60 minutes in the originating region; automated checks run at 5m intervals. 2) Ramp phase: if canary passes, ramp to 10% for 2 hours. 3) Global step: 50% for 4 hours if stable, then 100% completion. Gate checks include: a) error budget burn rate over the last 30m must be <= 3x baseline; b) p95 latency increase vs baseline must be <= 20% absolute or <= 50ms (whichever is larger) for interactive_chat, <= 30% for other classes; c) p99 regressions must be < 2x baseline and not exceed defined absolute caps per class; d) availability degradation must not exceed one-third of remaining error budget. If any check fails, automated rollback to previous version and trigger an incident runbook. Manual override allowed only with SRE approval and documented justification.
canary_observation_criteria: Metrics to evaluate during canary: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency per workload class, 5xx rate, qps-by-tenant (top 10), CPU/GPU utilization on serving nodes, KV-cache hit rate, and tail latency per hardware profile. Statistical anomaly detection (z-score threshold 3) plus fixed thresholds above should be used. The canary job must have automated log collection and a synthetic probe suite that exercises common prompt patterns; synthetic error budget is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SLO matrix documented and published in the Console and Confluence. 2) Automated rollout policy encoded in the orchestration layer (canary->ramp->global) with the checks above implemented and unit-tested. 3) Dashboards: per-workload-class SLI dashboard with 30d rolling burn, per-region breakdown, and per-tenant top contributors. 4) Alerts: automated paging when burn-rate > 5x baseline or remaining error budget < 20%. 5) Runbooks: completed rollback and postmortem templates linked to the orchestration actions. 6) End-to-end test: a staged rollout against a mirrored traffic generator that demonstrates automated rollback on an injected p95 regression of 40% for interactive_chat. 7) Legal/enterprise SLA clauses updated to reference workload-class targets for Enterprise customers.
out_of_scope: Dedicated private-contract renegotiation, billing model changes, and per-tenant custom SLO contracts for Enterprise (handled as separate sales/legal engagements). Deep changes to kernel scheduling optimizations are out of scope for this ticket and will be captured as engineering follow-ups.
open_questions: 1) Should synthetic probes count against the customer's error budget or a separate internal synthetic budget? 2) Acceptable maximum time window for automated rollback verification during ramp phases? 3) Are there established baseline variances per region/hardware profile we should parameterize into the gate logic?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative gates slow legitimate rollouts. Mitigation: allow per-project adjustable ramp timings and safe manual overrides with audit logs. Risk: noisy SLIs due to transient infra events. Mitigation: use rolling windows, median smoothing, and anomaly detection combined with absolute thresholds.
implementation_notes: Partner teams: SRE (orchestration integration), Observability (dashboards/alerts), Runtime (SLI instrumentation), Legal (SLA wording). Deliverables: Confluence PRD, orchestration PR with gate code, dashboard panels, synthetic probe definitions, and updated SLA appendix for Enterprise. Provide feature flag to enable new gate logic for a pilot customer cohort.
links: Confluence: /redwood/operational-slos/prd-dynamic-slos | Orchestration RFC: github.com/redwood/orch/rfcs/21 | Dashboards: grafana/redwood/slo-workload-matrix | Runbook template: drive.redwood.com/runbooks/slo-rollback-template
notes: This ticket intentionally defines conservative numeric caps for p99 and absolute latency increases to reduce customer-visible regressions. Engineering may propose tighter bounds after baseline noise characterization. The final SLO numbers will be ratified in a cross-team review called out in the project plan.
